chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Supplication repels the affliction that has descended and what has not yet descended.'

key_terms.الدُّعَاء: Supplication (du'a) — the act of calling upon God; a central devotional act in Islam
key_terms.النَّازِل: The descended — that which has already come down or befallen
key_terms.الْبَلَاء: Affliction/trial (bala') — calamity, tribulation, or divine test

ai.seo_question: Can du'a (supplication) repel affliction and calamity according to Imam Zayn al-Abidin?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) reports that Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) regularly taught that du'a (supplication) has the power to repel affliction both after it has already descended upon a person and before it arrives. This hadith belongs to the theological tradition affirming that divine decree is not fixed immutably, and that human invocation and worship can alter what befalls us. The fourth Imam's consistent repetition of this teaching ('used to say') indicates it was a core principle of his religious instruction.
word_analysis: the descended/that which has come down
